Saved to `recommendations.json` (valid JSON).

| Stage | Level | Why |
|---|---|---|
| prototype | 4 | Disposable code, zero blast radius, speed is everything. |
| proof-of-concept | 3 | Must survive a live demo; you'll debug it in front of an audience. |
| mvp | 3 | Real users, but thin tests and fast iteration — with level-2 review on auth, payments, PII, infra. |
| production | 2 | Paying customers + on-call team: AI output gets the same line-by-line read as an outside contributor's PR. |
| critical | 1 | Human authorship and traceability per line; AI drafts and critiques, a qualified engineer owns the code of record. |

The principle behind the ladder: vibe coding trades future understanding for present speed, so you spend it only where the future is short. The two notes in the summary — never accept code you couldn't debug tonight, and never let unreviewed code touch credentials/payments/PII/production infra — are what keep level 3 safe at MVP.

One deliberate call worth flagging: I put MVP and PoC at the same level (3) and made production stricter (2), rather than a straight 4/3/2/1/0. MVP code is mostly low-risk glue where line-by-line review is poor value, whereas production carries maintenance and customer-trust costs that justify the stricter default. If your team's MVPs routinely handle payments or health data, I'd drop `mvp` to 2.
